title: How a Believer Responds to Financial Hardship | PODCAST | Sh. Ahmed Umar #AMAU
description:
A man told the Sheikh he had $240,000 available on credit cards. After losing his job, he returned with $40,000 in debt. But what if you always pay your card off on time? Why does the Sheikh still warn against it?

In Episode 2 of The Believer’s Response, Sheikh Ahmed Umar joins Brother Shahid Hassan to discuss the money decisions facing Muslim households: buying a home, paying for university and finding better ways to earn without relying on Riba.

They examine the Prophet’s ﷺ guidance on the best ways to earn wealth, overlooked means of increasing rizq, and why helping others matters even when you are struggling yourself.

The discussion also asks why financial relief may be delayed despite your du’a, and how to start putting things right if your finances already involve riba.

Because sometimes the real question isn’t:

Surah Al-Burooj gives an answer that is far more unsettling - and far more hopeful - than simply saying, “Be patient.” The believers of the trench were tortured for one reason: they believed in Allah. Their enemies watched them burn. Yet right in the middle of this horrifying account, Allah describes Himself as Al-‘Azeez, Al-Hameed - the Almighty, the One worthy of all praise.

Why would Allah mention His absolute power at the very moment the believers appear powerless?

And what if the people we think are “winning” have misunderstood victory completely?

In this Tafseer Juz Amma episode, Sheikh Muhammad Tim Humble unpacks the story of the people of the trench, why Allah sometimes allows oppressors to have power, what their apparent success really means, and why Muslim suffering should force us to look at something much closer to home.

But Surah Al-Burooj does not only speak about what happens to the oppressed. It also reveals what the Ummah must do when surrounded by weakness, persecution and defeat.

title: Tafseer Surah An-Naziat: What Are You Living For? Dunya Or Akhirah? | #4 Tafseer Juz Amma #AMAU
description:
One day, your soul will be taken. No delay. No negotiation. It will simply be taken. The question is what it leaves behind. Allah reminds us in this Surah that you cannot hold on to both when they clash. Either the Dunya comes first, or the Akhirah does. There is no third option.

In this episode of Tafseer Juz Amma, Ustadh Muhammad Tim Humble walks through Tafseer of Surah An-Nazi'at, a Surah about the Resurrection, the reality of what comes after, and the choices that define which side you land on.

We reflect on the angels, the power of Allah over life and death, and the story of Musa and Fir'awn. A man who saw the signs clearly. Who was given every chance. And who still chose arrogance over submission. That's not just history. It's a mirror.

If Allah created the heavens without a single flaw, bringing you back to life is simple. The question was never whether it would happen. The question is what you did before it did.

Near the end of this Surah, a companion asked the Prophet ﷺ the same question people have always asked, when is the Hour? The Prophet ﷺ turned it back on him. One question. Three words. And it changes everything about how you're supposed to be living right now.
